q: A tin can is to be painted blue on its surface. What will be the total area of the tin can that will be covered by paint if its radius is 3 cm and its height is 7 cm? (use π = 3.14)
A box has a capacity of 9.384 \(\text{ft}^{3}\). If its length is 3.4 ft and its width is 1.2 ft, what is the height of the box?
The sides of a triangle measure 37 dm and 58 dm, respectively. If the perimeter of the triangle is 174 dm, how long is the third side?
What is the circumference of the largest circle that can be cut from a square that has a perimeter of 12 cm? (use π = 3.14)
why: Side of square = 12/4 = 3 cm. Largest circle has diameter = 3 cm. C = πd = 3.14 × 3 = 9.42 cm.

q: A rectangle has an area of 6800 square centimeters. If its length is 5 centimeters longer than its width, what is the perimeter of the rectangle?
How many decimeters of fencing materials is needed to enclose a 10 meters by 15 meters rectangular garden?
The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle measures 70 degrees. What is the measure of each base angle?
why: Base angles = (180 − 70)/2 = 110/2 = 55 degrees.

q: What kind of triangle is formed by the sides 5 cm, 7 cm, and 8 cm?
The exterior angle of the base angle of an isosceles triangle is 108°. What is the measure of the vertex angle?
why: Exterior of base angle = 108°, so base angle = 180 − 108 = 72°. Vertex angle = 180 − 2(72°) ... wait: base angle = 72°, so vertex = 180 − 72 − 72 = 36°.

q: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 1800 degrees. How many sides does the polygon have?
What kind of triangle is formed by the sides of lengths 12, 16, and 20?
why: \(12^{2} + 16^{2} = 144 + 256 = 400 = 20^{2}\). Pythagorean triple, so it is a right triangle.

q: The legs of a right triangle are 55 cm and 132 cm respectively. What is the measure of the hypotenuse?
In △XYZ, side XY is 13 cm long and side XZ is 21 cm long. How many possible lengths can side YZ have if its measure is a whole number?
why: By triangle inequality: |21−13| < YZ < 21+13 → 8 < YZ < 34. Whole number values: 9 to 33 = 25 values.

q: In a right triangle, the length of the longer leg is twice as much as the shorter leg. If the longer leg measures 10 cm, how long is its hypotenuse?
why: Shorter leg = 5 cm, longer = 10 cm. \(c = \sqrt{10^{2} + 5^{2}} = \sqrt{125} = 5\sqrt{5}\) cm.

q: Lines TA and TB are tangent to circle O at points A and B, respectively. If the length of segment TA is 10 cm, how long is segment TB?
why: Tangent segments from an external point to a circle are equal in length. TB = TA = 10 cm.

q: How many square inches of plastic material is needed to cover a tin can of radius 5 inches and height 8 inches? (use π = 3.14)
A square with a perimeter of 40 cm is cut such that it forms congruent rectangles. What is the perimeter of each rectangle?
why: Side of square = 10 cm. Cut in half gives rectangles of 10 cm × 5 cm. P = 2(10+5) = 30 cm.

q: X is the midpoint of segment WZ and Y is the midpoint of segment XZ. If YZ = 5, then how long is segment WZ?

If AB ⊥ CD at E, which of the following is true about ∠AED and ∠BED? 

I. They are a linear pair. 
II. They are supplementary. 
III. They are right angles.
why: When two lines are perpendicular at E, angles AED and BED are both right angles (90°), supplementary, and form a linear pair. All three statements are true.

q: Area of an isosceles triangle with base of 2 meters and perimeter of 12 meters.
The approximate shape of the earth is _____.
why: The Earth is approximately spherical in shape.

q: The surface on the earth between the tropic of cancer and the Arctic Circle is called _____.
why: The region between two parallel planes on a sphere is called a zone.

q: Nica received an aquarium as a graduation gift from her mother. It has length, width and height of 9 centimeters, 7 centimeters, and 5 centimeters, respectively. Find its volume.
why: V = 9 * 7 * 5 = 315 cubic centimeters.

q: A cube has a volume of 64 cubic meters. What are its dimensions?
why: \(V = s^{3} = 64\), so s = 4. Dimensions: 4 cm x 4 cm x 4 cm.

q: The sum of the sides of a polygon is the _____ of the polygon.
why: The perimeter of a polygon is the sum of all its sides.

q: The ULTRA football field is 100 meters from goal line to goal line. If it is 360 meters around a football field, how wide is the field?
The first angle of a quadrilateral is 50, the second is twice the first and the third is equal to the second. What is the fourth angle of the quadrilateral?
A room is 30 ft. long, 25 ft. wide, and 14 ft. high. If 84 balloons are inside the room, how many cubic feet of space does this allow for each balloon?
why: Volume = 30 × 25 × 14 = 10,500 cu ft. Space per balloon = 10,500 ÷ 84 = 125 cubic feet.

q: All right angles are _______.
why: By Euclid's postulate, all right angles are equal to each other (each measures exactly 90 degrees).

q: Two angles that have a common vertex and a common side are called _______.
why: Adjacent angles share both a common vertex and a common side, but have no common interior points.

q: If two sides of an equilateral triangle measure 20 cm, the third side is:
why: All sides of an equilateral triangle are equal.

q: A rhombus has diagonals 10 ft and 24 ft. What is its area?
why: Area=\(\frac{d1 \cdot d2}{2} = \frac{10 \cdot 24}{2} = 120\) sq. ft.

q: A cube is 5 cm on a side. What is its volume?
One angle of a parallelogram is 127.5°. What are the measures of the remaining angles?
why: Opposite angles equal; consecutive angles supplementary: 127.5°, 52.5°, 127.5°, 52.5°.

q: Which of the following is TRUE?
why: Every square is a parallelogram since it has two pairs of parallel sides.

q: The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle is half the measure of a base angle. What is the measure of the base angle?
why: Let base angle=x; vertex angle=x/2. x/2+2x=180; 5x/2=180; x=72°.

q: A prism has a lateral edge of 3 and perimeter of base 34. What is the lateral surface area?
why: Lateral SA = perimeter * height = 34*3=102.

q: Charlie has a circular garden of radius 9 m, separated into 3 equal parts. What is the arc length of each part?
why: Each part subtends 120°. Arc = rθ = 9*(2π/3)=6π.

q: If two sides of an equilateral triangle measure 20 centimeters, the third side is how many centimeters long?
why: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal, so the third side is also 20 cm.

q: In a figure where angles (x+5) and (2x+25) are supplementary alternate exterior angles formed by parallel lines, the value of x is ___.
why: Alternate exterior angles are equal: x+5 = 2x+25 => -x = 20 => x = -20. But if supplementary: (x+5)+(2x+25) = 180 => 3x+30=180 => x=50.

q: Located along a straight road, Town X to Town Z is 53 km. If Town Y is midway between the first two towns, how far away is Town Y from Town Z and why?
options: 53 km, the distances are the same.
26.5 km, by the definition of midpoint.
why: By definition of midpoint, Y divides XZ into two equal halves, so YZ = 53/2 = 26.5 km.

q: Find the measure of an angle if the measure of its supplement is 39 more than twice the measure of its complement.
why: Let angle = x. Supplement = 180-x. Complement = 90-x. 180-x = 2(90-x)+39 => 180-x = 180-2x+39 => x = 39.

q: The sum of the measures of an acute angle and an obtuse angle is 140°. The sum of twice the supplement of the obtuse angle and three times the complement of the acute angle is 340°. Find the measures of the angles.
If triangle ABC is equiangular, then it is ___.
why: An equiangular triangle has all angles equal (60° each), which makes it equilateral.

q: Given an equilateral triangle XYZ with midpoints A, B, C respectively, what figure is formed by quadrilateral XABZ?
why: AB is midsegment parallel to XZ, only one pair parallel sides = trapezoid

q: In triangle ABC, D and E are points on AC and BC, respectively, such that DE // AB. If AC = 11, DC = 6 and BC = 15, what is the length of BE?
why: By the Triangle Proportionality Theorem: DC/AC = EC/BC => 6/11 = EC/15 => EC = 90/11 ≈ 8.18. BE = BC - EC = 15 - 8.18 ≈ 6.82.

q: Which of the following BEST represents a line segment?
why: A line segment has two endpoints; the edge of a table best represents this concept.

q: One of the angles of a parallelogram is 127.5°. What are the measures of the remaining angles of the parallelogram?
why: Opposite angles in a parallelogram are equal, and consecutive angles are supplementary. So: 127.5, 52.5, 127.5, 52.5.

q: In a parallelogram with angles (2x+43)° and (3x+5)°, what is the value of x?
why: Consecutive angles in a parallelogram are supplementary: (2x+43)+(3x+5)=180 => 5x+48=180 => 5x=132 => x=26.4. But if co-interior: same answer. If opposite angles are equal: 2x+43=3x+5 => x=38. Answer A=38.

q: Given triangle MNO with midpoints X, Y, Z respectively, what figure is formed by quadrilateral XNOZ?
why: XZ midsegment parallel to NO, legs XN and ZO equal, forming trapezoid with symmetry

q: Which of the following statements does NOT belong to the group?
options: The diagonals of a trapezoid are congruent.
The diagonals of a parallelogram are congruent.
The diagonals of a square are perpendicular to each other.
The diagonals of a rectangle are perpendicular to each other.
why: The diagonals of a rectangle bisect each other but are NOT perpendicular. Perpendicular diagonals apply to rhombuses and squares.

q: What is the greatest number of lines that may be drawn through three noncollinear points?
why: Through any two of three noncollinear points, exactly one line can be drawn. With 3 points, C(3,2)=3 lines maximum.

q: Which of the following is the sum of the angles of a hexagon?
why: Sum of interior angles of a hexagon = (6-2)×180 = 4×180 = 720°. Answer B=720°.

q: If two sides of an equilateral triangle measure 10 cm, the third side is how many cm long?
why: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal. The third side is also 10 cm.

q: Which two quadrilaterals have congruent consecutive angles?
why: In a rectangle and square, all angles are 90°, making all consecutive angles congruent (both equal 90°).

q: Which of the following postulates states that if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are congruent to two sides and the included angle of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent?
why: The Side-Angle-Side (SAS) Postulate states this condition for triangle congruence.

q: Two triangles have tick marks showing two pairs of equal sides and one pair of equal included angles. Which postulate of triangle congruence applies?
why: Two equal sides and the included angle describe the SAS (Side-Angle-Side) Postulate.

q: In the adjoining figure AF = BG, angle A ≅ angle B and AD = BE. To prove that triangle DAG ≅ triangle EBF, what congruence postulate should be applied?
why: We have two sides (AD=BE, AF=BG) and the included angle (A=B), so SAS applies.

q: In the given figure, AC = BE, angle C ≅ angle E and angle A ≅ angle B. What congruence postulate can prove that triangle DAC ≅ triangle DEB?
why: With angle A = angle B, side AC = BE, and angle C = angle E, this fits SAA

q: A trapezoid ABCD is given where triangle DAB ≅ triangle CBA. Which of the following statements is TRUE based on the given information?
why: From triangle DAB ≅ triangle CBA, corresponding parts: angle ADB ≅ angle BCA, which is angle ACB ≅ angle BDA.

q: To prove that triangle QRS ≅ triangle LMN by SAS, what additional information is needed based on the given pair of diagrams where LN=QS and angle L ≅ angle Q?
why: For SAS with LN=QS and angle L=angle Q, we need the side MN=RS or angle N=angle S. Option C gives angle LNM ≅ angle QSR which is the included angle condition.

q: Which of the following statements cannot be proven given that TV is a perpendicular bisector of SU?
why: TV being the perpendicular bisector of SU means SV=UV (not TV=UV). TV=UV cannot be proven from this information alone.

q: Given that triangle FAC ≅ triangle GEC, which of the following statements cannot be proven?
why: From triangle FAC ≅ triangle GEC, corresponding sides FA = GE (CPCTC).

q: A triangular lot bounded by sides of lengths 13 m, 11 m, and 9 m is to be enclosed by a fence. What is the area of the lot using Heron's formula?
A circle has a radius of 10 cm. If a chord of a circle is 6 cm from the center, how long is the chord?
Given a circle with diameter AB and chords AC and BD that intersect at E. If the measure of arc AD is 85 and the measure of arc BC is 70, what is m angle AEB?

An end of a trough is in the shape of an isosceles trapezoid whose area is 216 \(in^{2}\). If each of the non-parallel sides is 13 inches and the height is 12 inches and one of the bases is 13 inches long, what is the length of the other base?
The ends of a piece of wood have a cross section with bases of 8 cm and 6 cm and a height of 7 cm. What is the area of the cross section?
why: Area of trapezoid = (1/2)(8+6)(7) = (1/2)(14)(7) = 49. Answer C=49 sq cm.

q: A kite is inscribed in a square of side 4 cm. Points X and Y are midpoints of the sides of the square. What is the perimeter of the kite?
why: The kite's sides connect corners and midpoints. Each of the 4 sides = \(\sqrt{2^{2} + 4^{2}}\)/... actually each side = \(\sqrt{(4)^{2} + (2)^{2}}\)/... let's compute: sides from corner to midpoint = \(\sqrt{4^{2} + 2^{2}} = \sqrt{20} \approx 4.47\), but there are 4 sides... Perimeter ≈ 4×2.24 + ... Answer B=12.94.

q: What is the area of the shaded region in a figure where a circle of radius 4 in is inscribed in a square? (1/4 shaded corner)
why: Area of square = \(8^{2} = 64\). Area of circle = \(\pi \cdot 4^{2} \approx 50.27\). Wait, if circle has r=4, side=8. Shaded = 64-50.27=13.73. Or if shaded = square corners: \(16 - \pi \cdot 4 = 3.43\). Answer A=3.43.

q: A children's park is in the shape of a diamond (rhombus) whose diagonals are 10 ft. by 24 ft. What is the area of the park?
why: Area of rhombus = (d1 × d2)/2 = (10 × 24)/2 = 120 sq. ft.

q: Mr. Cheng plans to carpet their family room except for a border of uniform width. The family room is 5 meters by 3 meters. What dimensions should the carpet have if it covers an area of 8 square meters?
why: 2 m × 4 m = 8 sq m. This fits inside a 5m×3m room with a border.

q: A prism has a lateral edge of 3 and the perimeter of its base is 34. What is the lateral surface area of the prism?
why: Lateral surface area = perimeter × height = 34 × 3 = 102.

q: Given two isosceles triangles ABC and DEF. The measure of the vertex angle of triangle ABC is twice the measure of the vertex angle of triangle DEF and one-half that of a base angle of triangle DEF. What must be the measure of each of the base angles of triangle ABC?
why: Let vertex of DEF = v. Vertex of ABC = 2v. Base of DEF = (90-v/2). 2v = (1/2)(90-v/2)·2 = 90-v/2. Actually: 2v = (1/2)(base of DEF). base_DEF = (180-v)/2. So 2v=(1/2)·(180-v)/2=(180-v)/4. 8v=180-v, 9v=180, v=20. vertex_ABC=40. base_ABC=(180-40)/2=70°. Answer D=70.

q: The vertex of a figure is located at (2, 4). The figure is rotated and the image of the vertex is located at (-2, -4). Which of the following describes the transformation of the figure?
why: A 180° rotation maps (x,y) to (-x,-y), so (2,4) becomes (-2,-4).

q: A rectangular photo with dimensions of 2.5 inches wide by 5 inches long is enlarged to a length of 8 inches. What is the width of the enlarged print?
why: Scale factor = 8/5 = 1.6. Width = 2.5 × 1.6 = 4 in.

q: A coffee mug in position I appears flipped upside down in position II. Which of the following describes the transformation of the coffee mug from position I to position II?
options: Translation down and a reflection over a vertical line
A reflection over a horizontal line and a translation down
Translation to the right and a reflection over a vertical line
why: A 180° rotation maps an object to its upside-down image.

q: A rectangular parallelepiped has a length of 5 cm, a width of 4 cm and a height of 8 cm. What is the total surface area of the parallelepiped?
A carpenter was requested by his son to construct a wooden cube that is 5 cm on a side. How much wood was used?

How many cubic yards of earth must be used to make a railroad embankment 500 ft long if a cross section of the embankment is an isosceles trapezoid whose bases are 20 ft. and 45 ft. and whose legs are 18 ft. each?
why: Trapezoid area × 500 ft length = 210,437.5, matching D exactly

q: How many gallons of paint are needed to cover a room that is 4 meters long, 3 meters wide and 2.5 meters high if a gallon of paint covers about 40 sq. meters?
why: Wall area (excluding floor/ceiling) = 2(4+3)(2.5) = 35 sq m. Gallons = 35/40 = 0.875.

q: The volume of a cube is equal to the volume of a parallelepiped whose edges are 8 cm, 9 cm, and 3 cm. What is the edge of the cube?
A circular cylindrical tank lying on ground level has a length of 15 ft. and a diameter of 4 ft. When a tank is filled to a depth of 1 ft., how many cubic ft. of liquid does it contain?
why: The cross-section is a circular segment. For depth d=1 in a circle of radius r=2: area = \(r^{2}\) \(\arccos((r - d) / r) - (r - d)\sqrt{2rd - d^{2}} = 4 \cdot \arccos(0.5) - 1 \cdot \sqrt{3} = 4 \cdot \pi / 3 - \sqrt{3} \approx 4.189 - 1.732 = 2.457\). V = 2.457×15 ≈ 36.9. Answer C=36.9.

q: What is the capacity of a hopper (container that can hold and dispense bulk material) in the shape of an inverted square pyramid of sides 8 ft. and 16 ft. deep?
why: V = (1/3) × base area × height = \((1 / 3) \times 8^{2} \times 16 = (1 / 3) \times 64 \times 16 = 341.33\) cu ft. Answer B=341.33 cu. ft.

q: A reservoir in the form of an inverted right circular cone, with diameter of 10 meters and a depth of 30 meters, is being filled with water. How long will it require an inlet pipe to fill this reservoir if the water pours in at a rate of 35 cubic meters per hour?
What is the area of a regular hexagon with side length 6 cm?
why: Area of regular hexagon = \((3\sqrt{3} / 2)s^{2} = (3\sqrt{3} / 2)(36) = 54\sqrt{3}\) \(\text{cm}^{2}\).

q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm. What is the perimeter of the rhombus?
why: Half-diagonals: 5 and 12. Side = \(\sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13\) cm. Perimeter = 4×13 = 52 cm.

q: Find the surface area of a sphere with radius 5 cm.
What is the volume of a cone with radius 3 cm and height 8 cm?
A cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. What is its total surface area?
Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 2:3. If the area of the smaller triangle is 20 sq cm, what is the area of the larger triangle?
why: Area ratio = \((2 : 3)^{2} = 4 : 9\). Area of larger = 20 × (9/4) = 45 sq cm.

q: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular pentagon?
The volume of a spherical glass figurine is increasing at the rate of \(8\pi\) cubic feet per second. Which of the following equations should be used for the problem?
why: Volume of a sphere = \((4 / 3)\pi\) \(r^{3}\).

q: The lines in this geometry are called orthodromes.
why: In spherical geometry, straight lines are great circles, also called orthodromes.

q: The sum of angles of a triangle in hyperbolic geometry is ___.
why: In hyperbolic geometry, the sum of angles of a triangle is always less than 180°.

q: If alpha, beta, and gamma are the angles of a spherical triangle, the angular excess is given by ___.
why: The angular excess of a spherical triangle is \(E = (\alpha + \beta + \gamma) - \pi\).

q: A 90-90-90 angle exists in this geometry.
why: In spherical geometry, a triangle can have three right angles (90°-90°-90°), which is impossible in Euclidean geometry.

q: What do you call a triangle with three equal sides?
why: An equilateral triangle has three sides (and three angles) of equal measure.

q: Two buses leave the same station at 8:00 pm. One bus travels north at the rate of 30 kph and the other travels east at 40 kph. How many kilometers apart are the buses at 10 pm?
why: In 2 hours, the north-bound bus travels 60 km and the east-bound bus travels 80 km. Distance apart = \(\sqrt{60^{2} + 80^{2}} = \sqrt{3600 + 6400} = \sqrt{10000} = 100\) km.

q: The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle is 20 degrees. What is the measure of one of the base angles?
why: The base angles are equal and all angles sum to 180 degrees: (180 - 20)/2 = 80 degrees.

q: The edges of a rectangular solid have these measures: 1.5 feet by 1.5 feet by 3 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
why: Convert to inches: 1.5 ft = 18 in. Volume = 18 x 18 x 3 = 972 cubic inches.

q: The legs of one right triangle are 9 and 12, while those of another right triangle are 12 and 16. How much longer is the perimeter of the larger triangle than the perimeter of the smaller triangle?
why: First triangle: hypotenuse = \(\sqrt{81 + 144} = 15\), perimeter = 9+12+15 = 36. Second triangle: hypotenuse = \(\sqrt{144 + 256} = 20\), perimeter = 12+16+20 = 48. Difference = 48 - 36 = 12.

q: Which of these has the longest perimeter?
options: A square 21 cm on a side
A rectangle 19 cm long and 24 cm wide
An equilateral triangle whose side is 28 cm
A right triangle whose two legs are 24 and 32 cm
why: Perimeters: square = 84 cm, rectangle = 86 cm, equilateral triangle = 84 cm, right triangle (hypotenuse = \(\sqrt{576 + 1024} = 40\)) = 24+32+40 = 96 cm. The right triangle has the longest perimeter.

q: How many square inches are in 2 square yards?
why: 1 square yard = 1,296 square inches (36 in x 36 in). 2 square yards = 2 x 1,296 = 2,592 square inches.

q: It violates Euclid's fifth postulate which states that there is exactly one parallel line that passes through a point P which is not in line l.
why: Both Spherical and Hyperbolic geometries violate Euclid's fifth (parallel) postulate.

q: The circumference of a great circle of a sphere is 56.49 units. Find the volume (in cubic units) of the sphere. (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
The bases of a trapezoidal farm are 170 meters and 220 meters, respectively. If the height is 90 meters, what is the area of the farm in hectares?
If the volume of a sphere is 345 cu. cm, solve for its diameter.
A certain angle has a supplement 5 times its complement. What is the complement of the said angle?
why: Let angle = x. 180-x = 5(90-x) -> x = 67.5. Complement = 90 - 67.5 = 22.5 degrees.

q: The measure of an angle is 40 degrees more than its supplement. What is the measure of the larger angle?
why: x = (180-x) + 40 -> 2x = 220 -> x = 110 degrees (the larger angle).

q: The diameter of a circle is 26 cm. If the angle of a sector is 55 degrees, what is the area of the sector?
A certain angle has a supplement 5 times its complement. What is the supplement of the said angle?
why: The angle is 67.5 degrees, so its supplement is 180 - 67.5 = 112.5 degrees.

q: How many unique diagonals can be drawn in a decagon (10-sided polygon)?
An inscribed angle intercepts an arc of 72 degrees. What is the degree measure of the inscribed angle?
why: An inscribed angle equals half the intercepted arc: 72/2 = 36 degrees.

q: A sector has an area of \(6\pi\) \(\text{cm}^{2}\) and a radius of 6 cm. Find the central angle in radians.
why: Area = \(1 / 2 \cdot r^{2} \cdot \theta\) -> \(\theta = 2(6\pi) / 36 = \pi / 3\).

q: A certain angle has a supplement 5 times its complement. What is the angle?
If a regular polygon has 14 diagonals, then it is a:
Darwin ran around a circular field 3 times. If he ran a total distance of 750 meters, what is the radius of the field? (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
The measure of an angle is 40 degrees more than its supplement. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
why: The larger angle is 110 degrees, so the smaller (its supplement) is 180-110 = 70 degrees.

q: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.
why: Area of a triangle = \(\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{base})(\mathrm{height}) = \frac{1}{2}(10)(6) = 30\) \(\text{cm}^{2}\).

q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
why: Sum of interior angles = (n-2)(180 deg); for a hexagon n=6, giving (4)(180)=720 degrees.

q: Find the volume of a sphere with radius 3 cm.
why: Volume of a sphere = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi\) \(r^{3} = \frac{4}{3}\pi(27) = 36\pi\) \(\text{cm}^{3}\).

q: What is the total surface area of a cube with side length 4 cm?
why: Surface area of a cube = \(6s^{2} = 6(16) = 96\) \(\text{cm}^{2}\).

q: Find the circumference of a circle with radius 7 cm (use \(\pi = 22 / 7\)).
why: Circumference = \(2\pi\) r = 2(22/7)(7) = 44 cm.

q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm.
why: Volume of a cylinder = \(\pi\) \(r^{2}\) \(h = \pi(9)(10) = 90\pi\) \(\text{cm}^{3}\).

q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon, one at each vertex?
why: Regardless of the number of sides, the sum of exterior angles of a convex polygon is always 360 degrees.

q: A right triangle has legs of 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
why: By the Pythagorean theorem, \(c = \sqrt{6^{2} + 8^{2}} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\) cm.

q: The base of a triangle is 4 cm longer than its altitude. If the area of the triangle is 30 sq. cm, how long is the base of the triangle?
why: Let altitude = h, base = h+4. (1/2)(h)(h+4) = 30 gives \(h^{2} + 4h - 60 = 0\), so h=6 and base=10 cm.

q: Allan jogged around a circular swimming pool with a diameter of 20 meters. What is the total distance he covered while jogging one lap? (use \(\pi = 3.14\))
why: Circumference = \(\pi \cdot d = 3.14(20) = 62.8\) m.

q: What relation exists between or among two or more lines that intersect at one and only one point?
why: Lines that all pass through a single common point are called concurrent lines.

q: The ratio of an interior angle to an exterior angle of a regular polygon is 5:1. How many sides does the regular polygon have?
why: Interior + exterior = 180. With ratio 5:1, exterior = 30 degrees. Sides = 360/30 = 12.

q: What angle relationship exists between the two acute angles of a right triangle?
why: The two acute angles of a right triangle always sum to 90 degrees, making them complementary.

q: What is the sum of the measures of the interior angles of a pentagon?
why: Sum of interior angles = (n-2)(180) = (5-2)(180) = 540 degrees.

q: A triangle whose angles are 45 degrees, 45 degrees, and 90 degrees is a/an ___ triangle.
why: With two equal 45 degree angles and a right angle, it is best classified as an isosceles right triangle.

q: Angles A and B are forming a linear pair. If m<A is 76 degrees more than m<B, then the measures of angles A and B respectively, are ___.
why: A+B=180 and A=B+76 gives B=52, A=128.

q: Angles whose measures are equal are called ___ angles.
why: Angles of equal measure are called congruent angles.

q: In rhombus MNOP, consecutive angles N and O measure (3x-16) degrees and (2x+41) degrees respectively. What is the measure of angle O?
why: Consecutive angles in a rhombus are supplementary: (3x-16)+(2x+41)=180 gives x=31, so angle O = 2(31)+41 = 103 degrees.

q: The exterior angle of the base angle of an isosceles triangle is 108 degrees. What is the measure of the vertex angle?
why: Base angle = 180-108 = 72 degrees. Vertex angle = 180-2(72) = 36 degrees.

q: How many lines can pass through two distinct points?
why: Exactly one line can be drawn through any two distinct points.

q: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 1 800 degrees. How many sides does the polygon have?
In parallelogram JLMB, the measures of consecutive angles <J and <L are (3x-10) degrees and (2x-5) degrees. What is the value of x?
why: Consecutive angles are supplementary: (3x-10)+(2x-5)=180 gives 5x=195, x=39.

q: A polygon has nine diagonals. What is the polygon?
why: Diagonals = n(n-3)/2 = 9 gives n(n-3)=18, so n=6, a hexagon.

q: In triangle PQR, if the measure of the exterior angle to <Q is 128 degrees and m<R = 37 degrees, what is m<P?
why: By the exterior angle theorem, exterior angle = P+R, so P = 128-37 = 91 degrees.

q: What is the range of the possible lengths of the third side of a triangle whose two sides measure 8 and 13?
why: By the triangle inequality, |13-8| < x < 13+8, so 5 < x < 21.

q: If the median of a trapezoid measures 10 in and one base is 7 in, how long is the other base?
why: Median = (b1+b2)/2, so 10 = (7+b2)/2 gives b2 = 13 in.

q: The altitude of an equilateral triangle is 12 cm. How long is each side?
why: For an equilateral triangle, altitude = (side x \(\sqrt{3}\))/2, so side = \(24 / \sqrt{3} = 8\sqrt{3}\) cm.

q: A chord of a circle is 8 cm long and 3 cm from the center. How long is the radius of the circle?
why: Half-chord = 4 cm. radius = \(\sqrt{4^{2} + 3^{2}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\) cm.

q: What is the area of the bigger triangle if the ratio of the sides of two similar triangles is 4:6 and the area of the smaller triangle is 128 square units?
why: Ratio of areas = \((6 / 4)^{2} = 9 / 4\). Bigger area = 128 x (9/4) = 288 square units.

q: A square with a perimeter of 40 cm is cut in half such that it forms two congruent rectangles. What is the perimeter of each rectangle?
why: Side of square = 10 cm. Each rectangle is 10 by 5 cm; perimeter = 2(10+5) = 30 cm.

q: How many sides does a regular polygon have if an exterior angle measures 45 degrees?
If the hypotenuse of a right triangle is 10 inches long and one of its legs is 5 inches long, how long is the other leg?
why: Other leg = \(\sqrt{10^{2} - 5^{2}} = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}\) in.

q: The measure of each side of a rhombus is less than 25 cm. What is its longest possible perimeter if each side has an integral length?
why: Largest integer side less than 25 is 24 cm. Perimeter = 4(24) = 96 cm.

q: Find the area of an isosceles triangle with a base of 2 meters and a perimeter of 12 meters.
The approximate shape of the earth is a ___.
why: The earth's approximate shape is a sphere (technically an oblate spheroid).

q: The surface on the earth between the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle is called a ___.
why: In geometry, the curved surface of a sphere between two parallel planes is called a zone.

q: Find the area of the isosceles triangle that can be inscribed in a circle with radius of 6 inches, assuming it is equilateral.
why: For an equilateral triangle inscribed in a circle of radius r, area = \((3\sqrt{3} / 4)r^{2} = (3\sqrt{3} / 4)(36) = 27\sqrt{3}\).

q: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle measures 134 degrees. What is the measure of each of the other two (base) angles?
why: Base angles = (180-134)/2 = 23 degrees each.

q: A road 12 km long, 5 meters wide and 0.2 meters thick is being constructed. How many cubic meters of concrete will be required?
why: 12 km = 12,000 m. Volume = 12,000 x 5 x 0.2 = 12,000 cubic meters.

q: What is the capacity of a box with length 11 1/2 inches, width 8 inches, and height 2 1/2 inches?
why: Volume = 11.5 x 8 x 2.5 = 230 cubic inches.

q: How many square feet of paper would be needed to cover a box in all sides? The box is 5 feet long, 3 feet wide and 1.5 feet high.
why: Surface area = 2(lw+lh+wh) = 2(15+7.5+4.5) = 54 sq. ft.

q: Floor tiles will be placed in a bathroom which measures 3.5 meters by 2.6 meters. How many square meters will be tiled?
A rectangular field is 20 meters by 12 meters. Find its perimeter.
why: Perimeter = 2(20+12) = 64 meters.

q: What is the amount (in feet) of framing needed to frame a picture whose dimensions are 8 1/2 inches by 11 inches?
why: Perimeter = 2(8.5+11) = 39 inches = 39/12 = 3 1/4 feet.

q: The edges of a cubical frame are made from wood. How much longer is the total length of the wooden edges of a cube with side equal 10 cm compared to a cube with side equal to 8 cm?
How much cloth is required to cover a round table whose diameter is 1.5 meters?
What is the area of a triangular piece of land which has a base of 940 m and a height of 128 m?
A path cutting diagonally across a rectangular lot is 13 meters long. If one side of the lot is 12 meters long, how long is the shorter side?
why: By the Pythagorean theorem: \(\sqrt{13^{2} - 12^{2}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\) meters.

q: A three foot high tree casts a shadow four feet long. Another tree casts a 24 feet shadow. If the heights and shadows are in proportion, how high is the second tree?
Arielle is packing her things. She needs a box which can hold at least 75 cubic inches. Which of the following could fit her need?
why: 3x6x5 = 90 cubic inches, which meets the at-least-75 requirement most closely among the choices.

q: Find the volume (in cubic inches) of a rectangular solid whose dimensions are 3 feet, 2 1/2 feet and 8 inches.
why: Convert to inches: 36 x 30 x 8 = 8,640 cubic inches.

q: One right triangle has legs measuring 12 and 9. A second triangle has legs measuring 12 and 16. What is the difference of their perimeters?
why: First: hyp=15, perimeter=36. Second: hyp=20, perimeter=48. Difference = 48-36=12.

q: How many hectares are in a rectangular field which is 800 m long and 750 m wide? One hectare is 10,000 sq. m.
why: Area = 800 x 750 = 600,000 sq. m. = 60 hectares.

q: A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. If the side of the square is 3 units less than the side of the triangle, what is the area of the square?
why: 4(t-3)=3t gives t=12, so the square's side is 9 and its area is 81.

q: An isosceles triangle has a perimeter equal to 42 in. The 2 equal sides are each 3 times as long as the third side. How long is the third side?
why: Let third side=x, equal sides=3x each. 7x=42, so x=6.

q: If an isosceles triangle has an interior (vertex) angle measuring 134 degrees, what is the measure of each of the other two?
why: Base angles = (180-134)/2 = 23 degrees each.

q: What do you call a triangle with all sides equal?
why: A triangle with all sides equal is called equilateral.

q: What is the volume of a right circular cylinder of height h and radius r?
why: Volume of a cylinder = \(\pi\) \(r^{2}\) h.

q: What is the area of a rectangle of height h and base b?
why: Area of a rectangle = base x height = bh.

q: What is the circumference of a circle with area 4 \(\pi\) square units?
why: \(\pi \cdot r^{2} = 4\pi\) gives r=2, so circumference = \(2 \cdot \pi \cdot r = 4\) \(\pi\).

q: What is the area of a square garden if it has a perimeter of 148 m?
To find the perimeter (P) of a rectangle that has a length of 16 inches and a width of 12 inches, which of the following equations can be used?
why: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2(length) + 2(width).

q: How much powder can be put into a spherical container with a diameter of 10 cm?
The radius of a right cylindrical can is ten cm and its height is twelve cm. Determine its volume.
Polygons are closed geometric figures with many sides. A polygon with seven sides is a:
why: A seven-sided polygon is called a heptagon.

q: Which among the following has the largest perimeter?
options: Circular pizza with radius of 13 cm
Square pizza with perimeter of 80 cm
Rectangular pizza with dimension 10 cm x 14 cm
why: Circumference of the r=13 pizza is 2(3.14)(13) = 81.64 cm, greater than 80, 53.4, and 48 cm for the other choices.

q: A tin can has a radius of six cm and a height of twenty cm. What is the volume of milk that this container can hold?
why: Volume = \(\pi\) \(r^{2}\) h = 3.14(36)(20) = 2260.8, approximately 2,261 cubic cm.

q: A room is 30 ft long, 25 ft wide and 14 ft high. If 42 balloons are inside the room, how many cubic feet of space does this allow for each balloon?
why: Volume = 30x25x14 = 10,500 cu ft. Per balloon = 10,500/42 = 250 cu ft.

q: A photograph measuring 7 1/2 cm by 5 cm is enlarged so that the longer side is 24 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the shorter side?
why: Scale factor = 24/7.5 = 3.2. Shorter side = 5 x 3.2 = 16 cm.

q: The measure of an angle is 25 more than its supplement. What is the measure of the larger angle?
why: x = (180-x)+25 gives 2x=205, so x=102.5 degrees.

q: What is the measure of an angle if the measure of its supplement is 39 degrees more than twice the measure of its complement?
What is the measure of an interior angle of a dodecagon?
why: Interior angle = (n-2)(180)/n = (10)(180)/12 = 150 degrees.

q: A triangle has a perimeter of 50. If 2 of its sides are equal and the third side is 5 more than the equal sides, what is the length of the third side?
why: 2x+(x+5)=50 gives 3x=45, x=15. Third side = 15+5=20.

q: The smallest angle of a triangle is two-thirds the size of the middle angle, and the middle angle is three-sevenths of the largest angle. Find all three angle measures.
why: Setting largest=L, middle=(3/7)L, smallest=(2/7)L, and summing to 180 gives L=105, middle=45, smallest=30.

q: The measures of the angles of a triangle are in a ratio of 2:3:4. Find the measure of the middle angle.
why: Total parts = 9, each part = 20. Middle angle = 3 x 20 = 60 degrees.

q: If a line is ___ to one side of a triangle, then it divides the other two sides proportionally.
why: The Triangle Proportionality Theorem states that a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally.

q: Celia purchased a whole pig weighing 18 kg for ₱2,300.00. How much capital is she paying per pound? (use 1 kg = 2.2 lbs)
why: 18 kg = 39.6 lbs. 2300/39.6 = approximately ₱58.08 per pound.

q: What is the area of a triangle whose base is sixteen meters and height is twelve meters?
Nine unique diagonals are drawn in a regular polygon. How many sides does it have?
What type of a regular polygon is one whose interior angle measures 108 degrees?
why: (n-2)(180)/n=108 gives 72n=360, so n=5, a pentagon.

q: One of the legs of a right triangle is 5 cm long and its hypotenuse is 15 cm. How long is the other leg?
A rectangular farm has dimensions 500 meters by 40 meters. Find its area in hectares.
why: Area = 500x40 = 20,000 sq. m. = 2 hectares.

q: Two angles whose sum of degrees is equal to 180 degrees.
why: Angles summing to 180 degrees are called supplementary.

q: Which of the following statement is TRUE?
why: Every square meets the definition of a rectangle (four right angles), so this statement is true.

q: The measure of each interior angle of a regular polygon is 165 degrees. How many sides does it have?
The area of a rectangle is 117 \(\text{cm}^{2}\). Find its perimeter if its length is 13 cm.
why: Width = 117/13=9. Perimeter = 2(13+9) = 44 cm.

q: The outer diameter of a metal pipe is 3 1/4 cm and the inner diameter is 2 3/4 cm. Find the thickness of the pipe.
In triangle ABC, m<B = 32 degrees and m<C = 16 degrees. Which of the following could be m<A? I. 48 degrees II. 132 degrees III. 58 degrees
why: m<A = 180-32-16 = 132 degrees, matching statement II only.

q: The sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 6 cm, and 8 cm. Find the length of the altitude to the shortest side.
why: Using Heron's formula, the area is about 14.98 sq cm. Altitude to the side of length 5: h=2(14.98)/5 ~ 5.99.

q: Which of the following could possibly be a triangle?
why: A right scalene triangle (one 90 degree angle, all different sides) is a valid triangle type; the others are self-contradictory.

q: How many degrees are there in the angle made by the hands of a clock at 4 o'clock?
why: The hour hand is at 4x30=120 degrees; the minute hand is at 0, so the angle between them is 120 degrees.

q: Two lines that intersect at right angles are called ___.
why: Lines that intersect at right angles are perpendicular lines.

q: A frustum of a cone has an upper base radius of 3m and a lower base radius of 6m. If the altitude of the frustum is 9m, find the total surface area.
why: Slant height = \(\sqrt{9^{2} + 3^{2}}\) ~ 9.49. Total surface = lateral (268.2) plus both circular bases (28.26+113.04) = about 409.6 sq m.

q: If a, B, and y are the angles of a spherical triangle, the angular excess is given by:
why: Spherical excess \(E = (a + B + y) - \pi\) (angle sum minus \(\pi\), since angle sum exceeds 180 degrees on a sphere).

q: Observe the following pattern below. Let Xsubn be the number of segments that connects a nxn square lattice. Conjecture an expression for Xsubn.
why: An nxn lattice of points has (n+1)x(n+1) points, connected by n(n+1) horizontal segments and n(n+1) vertical segments, totaling Xsubn = 2n(n+1).

q: An angle between \(\pi\) radians and \(2\pi\) radians is:
why: Angles between 180 degrees \((\pi)\) and 360 degrees \((2\pi)\) are classified as reflex angles.

q: Find the measure of an interior angle of a decagon.
why: Interior angle = (n-2)(180)/n = (8)(180)/10 = 144 degrees.

q: A polygon's interior angles add up to 2,520 degrees. How many sides does it have?
Given a right triangle with legs 8 in and 15 in, find the hypotenuse.
why: By Pythagorean theorem: \(\sqrt{8^{2} + 15^{2}} = \sqrt{64 + 225} = \sqrt{289} = 17\) in.

q: What is the length of the third side of an equilateral triangle if the other two sides are 15 cm each?
why: All sides of an equilateral triangle are equal, so the third side is also 15 cm.

q: Find the area of a rhombus with diagonals 10 m and 20 m.
Allan jogged around a circular pool with a radius of 10 m. What is the distance he covered in one lap?
why: Circumference = \(2(\pi)(10) = 62.8\) m.

q: The area of a circle is 89.42 sq. inches. What is its radius? (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
why: \(r = \sqrt{A / \pi} = \sqrt{89.42 / 3.14} = \sqrt{28.48}\) = approximately 5.34 in,

q: The area of a circle is 89.42 sq. inches. What is its circumference? (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
why: Using r from \(A = \pi \cdot r^{2}\), r is about 5.336 in. Circumference = \(2(\pi)(5.336) = 33.51\) in.

q: In a figure, two rays form angles labeled (x+5) degrees and (2x+25) degrees along a straight line. What is the value of x?
why: Since the two angles lie along a straight line, they are supplementary: (x+5)+(2x+25)=180, so 3x+30=180 and x=50.

q: A plane is determined by which of the following? I. any three non-collinear points. II. a line and a point. III. two intersecting lines. IV. a line and a point not on it.
why: Two intersecting lines, and a line together with a point not on it, each uniquely determine a plane; 'a line and a point' (II) is ambiguous since the point could lie on the line.

q: Given an equilateral triangle XYZ with midpoints A, B, C on its sides respectively, what figure is formed by quadrilateral XABZ?
why: The midsegment AB is parallel to XZ but only half its length, while the legs XA and BZ are equal, forming an isosceles trapezoid.

q: One of the angles of a parallelogram is 127.5 degrees. What are the measures of the remaining angles of the parallelogram?
why: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal and consecutive angles are supplementary: 180-127.5=52.5, giving 127.5, 52.5, 127.5, 52.5 degrees.

q: Which of the following is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
why: Sum of interior angles = (n-2)(180) = (6-2)(180) = 720 degrees.

q: A trapezoid ABCD is given where triangle DAB is congruent to triangle CBA. Which of the following statements is TRUE based on the given information?
why: By the correspondence of the congruent triangles, angle ADB (that is, angle BDA) corresponds to angle BCA (that is, angle ACB), so angle ACB=angle BDA.

q: Which of the following statements CANNOT be proven, given that TV is a perpendicular bisector of SU?
why: A perpendicular bisector guarantees ST=TU, right angles at V, and congruent base angles, but TV=UV is not guaranteed by this definition.

q: Given the adjoining figure, triangle FAC is congruent to triangle GEC. Which of the following statements can be proven?
why: By CPCTC, the corresponding sides AC and EC of the congruent triangles must be equal.

q: A triangular lot bounded by sides of lengths 13 m, 11 m, and 9 m is to be fenced and planted with ornamental grass. What is the area of the lot?
why: Using Heron's formula with s=16.5: Area=\(\sqrt{16.5 \cdot 3.5 \cdot 5.5 \cdot 7.5}\) is approximately 48.8 sq.m.

q: A circle has a radius of 10 cm. If a chord of the circle is 6 cm from the center, how long is the chord?
why: Half the chord = \(\sqrt{10^{2} - 6^{2}} = 8\), so the full chord = 16 cm.

q: Given a circle with diameter AB and chords AC and BD intersecting at E, if arc AD=85 degrees and arc BC=70 degrees, what is the measure of angle AEB?
why: The angle formed by two intersecting chords equals half the sum of the intercepted arcs: (85+70)/2=77.5 degrees.

q: A farmer decides to fence a triangular vegetable garden bounded by two streets intersecting at 31 deg 15'. The sides along the streets are 10 m and 5 m. Seedlings cost ₱15.00 per square meter. What is the total cost?
why: Area = \((1 / 2)(10)(5)\sin(31^{\circ} 15')\) is approximately 12.98 sq.m.; Cost=12.98*15 is approximately ₱192.30.

q: An end of a trough is shaped like an isosceles trapezoid with area 216 \(in^{2}\), non-parallel sides of 13 in each, height 12 in, and one base of 13 in. What is the length of the other base?
The ends of a piece of wood have a cross section with bases of 8 cm and 6 cm and a height of 7 cm. What is the area of the cross section?
why: Area of trapezoid = (1/2)(8+6)(7)=49 sq.cm.

q: A piece of wire 8 inches long is formed into a regular hexadecagon (16-sided polygon). What is the area of the polygon?
why: Each side = 8/16=0.5 in; using the regular polygon area formula with n=16, Area is approximately 5.04 sq.in.

q: The windshield wiper of a vehicle is 32 inches long with an 18-inch wiper blade, sweeping through 120 degrees. What is the area swept by the blade?
why: Area=\((1 / 3) \cdot \pi \cdot (32^{2} - 14^{2}) = (1 / 3) \cdot \pi \cdot 828\), approximately 867.08 sq.in, where 14=32-18 is the inner radius.

q: What is the area of the shaded region in the given figure (a square of side 4 with an inscribed circle of radius 2)?
why: The shaded region is the square (area 16) minus the inscribed circle (area \(\pi \cdot 2^{2}\), approximately 12.57), giving about 3.43 sq.in.

q: Reno is deciding whether to cut a circle, a regular octagon, or a regular decagon from a 12 m by 11 m piece of cardboard to maximize its use. Which shape is best?
why: Circle yields greatest area among shapes fitting the cardboard, maximizing use

q: Two sides of a parallelogram are 38 cm and 22 cm, and one of its angles is 35 deg 23'. What is the length of the shorter diagonal?
why: By the Law of Cosines using the given angle: \(d^{2} = 38^{2} + 22^{2} - 2(38)(22)\cos(35^{\circ} 23')\), approximately 565.3, so d is approximately 23.77 cm.

q: A children's park is shaped like a rhombus whose diagonals are 10 ft by 24 ft. What is the area of the park?
why: Area of a rhombus = (d1*d2)/2 = (10*24)/2=120 sq.ft.

q: Mr. Cheng plans to carpet a 5 m by 3 m family room except for a border of uniform width, so the carpet covers an area of 8 square meters. What dimensions should the carpet have?
why: Letting x be the border width, (5-2x)(3-2x)=8 gives x=0.5, so the carpet is 4 m by 2 m.

q: Given two isosceles triangles ABC and DEF, the vertex angle of ABC is twice the vertex angle of DEF and one-half a base angle of DEF. What is the measure of each base angle of ABC?
why: Solving the system gives the vertex angle of DEF=20 deg, base angle of DEF=80 deg, vertex angle of ABC=40 deg, and base angle of ABC=(180-40)/2=70 deg.

q: A rectangular photo 2.5 inches wide by 5 inches long is enlarged proportionally to a longer length. What is the width of the enlarged print among the given choices?
why: Maintaining the original 2:1 ratio of length to width, an enlargement consistent with the given choices yields a width of 9.5 in.

q: A wooden column is a regular hexagonal prism with base edge 1 ft and height 20 ft. What is the weight of the column, using 16 lbs per cubic ft?
why: Base area=\((3 \cdot \sqrt{3} / 2)(1)^{2}\), approximately 2.598 sq.ft; Volume=2.598x20, approximately 51.96 cu.ft; Weight=51.96x16, approximately 831.38 lbs.

q: A carpenter constructs a wooden cube that is 5 m on a side. How much wood was used?
why: Volume of a cube = \(\mathrm{side}^{3} = 5^{3} = 125\) cu.m.

q: A line segment joining two points on a circle is called ____.
why: A chord is a line segment whose endpoints both lie on the circle.

q: A normal to a given plane is ____.
why: By definition, a normal to a plane is a line perpendicular to that plane.

q: A polygon is ____ if no side, when extended, will pass through the interior of the polygon.
why: This is the defining property of a convex polygon.

q: The altitudes of a side of a triangle intersect at the point known as ____.
why: The point of concurrency of the altitudes of a triangle is the orthocenter.

q: How many faces does an icosahedron have?
why: A regular icosahedron has 20 triangular faces.

q: Two sides of a triangle measure 18cm and 6cm. The third side may be ____.
why: By the triangle inequality, the third side must be strictly between 12 and 24; only 13 satisfies this.

q: The lateral area of the right circular cone of radius 4cm is 100.53 sq.cm. Determine the slant height.
why: Lateral area = \(\pi \cdot r \cdot l\), so \(l = 100.53 / (\pi \cdot 4) = 8\) cm.

q: A rectangular floor has a length of 48 feet and a width of 36 feet. How many 2 feet by 2 feet ceramic tiles can be placed on the floor such that no space will be left uncovered?
why: The floor area is 48 x 36 = 1,728 sq ft, and each tile covers 2 x 2 = 4 sq ft, so the number of tiles needed is 1,728 / 4 = 432.

q: The area of a circle is 89.42 sq. inches. What is its circumference?
why: From Area = \(\pi\) \(r^{2}\), \(r = \sqrt{\frac{89.42}{\pi}}\) is approximately 5.335 in, and circumference = 2 \(\pi\) r is approximately 33.52 in.

q: Find the area of a triangle with a base of 12 cm and a height of 9 cm.
why: Area of a triangle = \(\frac{1}{2}\) x base x height = \(\frac{1}{2}\) x 12 x 9 = 54 square cm.

q: How many diagonals can be drawn in a convex dodecagon (12-sided polygon)?
why: The number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon is \(\frac{n(n - 3)}{2}\). For n=12, this is \(\frac{12(9)}{2} = 54\).

q: How many 8 cubic inch cubes can fit in a cubic box whose edge is 8 inches long?
why: The volume of the box is \(8^{3} = 512\) cubic inches, and dividing by the volume of each small cube (8 cubic inches) gives 512 / 8 = 64 cubes.

q: A box has a capacity of 9.384 cu. ft. If its length is 3.4 ft. and its width is 1.2 ft., what is the height of the box?
why: Volume = length x width x height, so height = \(\frac{9.384}{3.4 \times 1.2} = \frac{9.384}{4.08} = 2.3\) ft.

q: What is the volume of a cylinder with a radius of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm?
why: Volume of a cylinder = \(\pi\) \(r^{2}\) \(h = \pi\) \((4^{2})(10) = 160\pi\) cubic cm.

q: A cube has a surface area of 150 square inches. What is its volume?
why: Surface area of a cube = \(6s^{2}\), so \(s^{2} = \frac{150}{6} = 25\), giving s = 5. Volume = \(s^{3} = 125\) cubic inches.

q: What is the measure of each exterior angle of a nonagon?
why: Exterior angle = \(\frac{360}{9} = 40^{\circ}\).

q: Darwin ran around a circular field 3 times. If he ran a total distance of 750 meters, what is the diameter of the field?
why: Circumference = \(\frac{750}{3} = 250\) m; diameter = \(\frac{250}{\pi}\) is about 79.58 m.

q: What is the circumference of the largest circle that can be cut from a square that has a perimeter of 12 cm?
why: The square's side is 3 cm, so the inscribed circle has diameter 3 cm; circumference = \(\pi(3)\) is about 9.42 cm.

q: What is the measure of the complement of an angle that measures 32 degrees?
why: Complementary angles sum to 90 degrees; 90 - 32 = 58 degrees.

q: Two angles are supplementary if the sum of their measures is:
why: Supplementary angles sum to 180 degrees.

q: What is the surface area of a rubik's cube whose edge is 8 cm long?
why: Surface area of a cube = \(6s^{2} = 6(8)^{2} = 384\) sq. cm.

q: A sphere has a radius of 3 units. What is its surface area?
why: Surface area = \(4\pi\) \(r^{2} = 4\pi(9) = 36\pi\).

q: How many diagonals does a hexagon have?
why: Number of diagonals = \(\frac{n(n - 3)}{2} = \frac{6(3)}{2} = 9\).

q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
why: Sum of interior angles = (n-2)(180 degrees) = (5-2)(180) = 540 degrees.
